acknowledge.text: There's some spark in you right now. That's worth noticing.
A lot of energy in you right now. That's a good thing to have.
You're buzzing. Enjoy it, and maybe point some of it somewhere you care about.

understand.text: Good moments often fade faster than hard ones. Many people find it helps to pause on them on purpose.
This kind of feeling often follows progress, connection or something to look forward to. Knowing what brought it on makes it easier to find again.

options.title: What brought it on?
options.text: In a line: what happened just before you felt like this?
options.why: Knowing what lifts you can make it easier to find again.
options.prompt: What happened just before I felt like this:

options.title: Save it for a harder day
options.text: Write to yourself for a low day: what's true right now that you might forget then?
options.why: Your own words, from a good moment, can be easier to believe later.

options.title: Use the momentum
options.text: Pick one small thing you've been putting off and give it a few minutes while the energy's here.
options.why: Energy that gets used tends to feel good, rather than restless.

options.title: Share it
options.text: Tell someone about the good thing, not to impress anyone, just so it's heard.
options.why: Many people find that telling someone makes a good moment last a little longer.

options.title: Let it move
options.text: Put on a song you love and move however you like, for the length of it.
options.why: Moving with good energy is a way of enjoying it fully.

options.title: Catch your breath
options.text: If it feels like a lot, take three slow breaths before the next thing.
options.why: A short pause can help very high energy stay yours, rather than scattered.

options.title: Write down what's good
options.text: Three small things that are going right at the moment.
options.why: Writing good things down tends to help you notice more of them.
